name: noCRM
summary: Action-driven sales tool from France's Positive Group: every lead carries a next step instead of a form to fill in. 15-day trial, no free plan.
best_for: solo sellers, small outbound teams and telesales operations that want a list of leads each carrying a next step, rather than a CRM to configure — and European buyers who care that it is built and hosted in the EU, ISO 27001 certified and billed in euros
skip_if: you want email to live inside the tool without paying for the top tier, because Starter and Expert are BCC-only; you need WhatsApp, VoIP dialling or call recording, all of which are Dream-only; you are running a team and expected roles, permissions and performance reports below €33 a user a month; or you wanted a free plan rather than a 15-day trial
honest_knock: The pitch is that salespeople hate CRMs, and the answer is a tool built around the next action rather than the form. What the plan table shows is that almost everything a sales team needs to work that way sits on the top tier. Two-way email sync is Dream at €33 a user; on Starter and on Expert, email is BCC only, which means you copy noCRM on outgoing mail and read replies elsewhere. WhatsApp lead creation and conversation sync are Dream. The VoIP integrations the homepage leads with — CloudTalk, JustCall, Aircall, power dialling, call recording, transcripts — are Dream. Roles and permissions, lead assignment, team goal tracking and team performance reports are Dream. Internal automations are Dream. noCRM's own FAQ calls Expert "the best fit for most teams", and Expert has no team management in it at all. So the honest way to read the ladder is that Starter and Expert are versions for one person — a lead list with follow-ups, and then the same thing without the caps — while the product the marketing describes starts at €33 a user a month on annual billing, or €39 monthly. That is three times the entry price, and it is the number to budget from if more than one person is selling. Two smaller things. Starter is restricted to new customers, so it is not a tier you can fall back to when a year on Expert turns out to be more than you needed. And there is no free plan behind the trial: 15 days, or 30 if you hand over a card first.

plans.name: Starter
plans.includes: 500 leads in one pipeline, quick lead capture, prospecting lists, duplicate detection, categories and tags, up to 4 custom fields, smart follow-ups, calendar sync, mobile app, customisable call scripts, 5,000 emails a month, BCC-only email. New customers only.

plans.name: Expert
plans.includes: Adds unlimited leads and pipelines, unlimited custom fields, quotes and invoices, post-sales tasks, quick custom actions, 3,000+ Zapier automations, API access at 2,000 requests a day, standard webhooks and limited native integrations. Email is still BCC only.

plans.name: Dream
plans.includes: Adds two-way email sync with templates, shared inboxes and email tracking; WhatsApp lead creation and conversation sync; VoIP integrations with CloudTalk, JustCall and Aircall including power dialling, call recording and transcripts; internal automations; roles and permissions, team goal tracking and performance reports; unlimited native integrations; priority support and personalised onboarding from five users.

pricing.plans_source: hand-curated from the vendor's pricing page
pricing.notes: (read 9 September 2026 and re-read 14 October 2026 on www.nocrm.io/pricing, in both billing modes; unchanged) Three per-seat tiers and no free plan. The page opens on annual billing, where Starter is €11, Expert €22 and Dream €33 per user a month; switch the toggle to monthly and the same tiers are €19, €29 and €39. That makes the annual saving 42% on Starter, 24% on Expert and 15% on Dream, so the "save up to 40%" badge is carried entirely by the cheapest tier. Starter is capped at 500 leads in a single pipeline with at most four custom fields, and it is sold to new customers only. Every tier includes 5,000 emails a month and all users on one account must sit on the same plan. There is no free tier: a 15-day trial runs without a credit card, or 30 days if you add one, and the account is paused rather than downgraded when it ends. Checkout is through Stripe, and 20% VAT is added for French companies and for EU businesses without a valid VAT number. One thing to read twice — in the annual view the Starter card reads €11/user/year while the comparison table directly beneath it reads €11/user/month for the same plan. The month is the correct one: it is what the page's own plan data carries for every other tier and what the monthly figure of €19 is measured against.

compare_with.name: HubSpot
compare_with.why: the comparison most people arrive with, and the split is free against focused. HubSpot's CRM is free for up to two users and 1,000 contacts and grows into marketing, service and content hubs on the same contact database; noCRM has no free tier and no ambition to be those things. What you buy here is a narrower product — a pipeline, a next action on every lead, and follow-up reminders — with a per-seat price from €11 to €33 a month on annual billing. If nobody on the team will ever configure a CRM, that narrowness is the feature. If you want marketing automation in the same place, this is the wrong tool and the Positive group sells that separately.

sessions.what: Tested by our team on 23 October 2026 during the free trial, without a card and without connecting a mailbox, calendar or WhatsApp: Daan created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. We added three made-up leads, gave each a next action, moved one to the quotation step and typed a duplicate lead title without saving it.
findings: The workspace worked straight away without any connection. A pop-up offered a 30-day trial instead of 15 days if we entered payment details that day; we declined. The welcome tour ('Let's create our first lead') came back on every page load, even with three leads in place.

Three leads took about three minutes. The New lead form has a title, a contact block (first name, last name, phone and email as a text template), step, amount, probability, an expected closing date that defaults to tomorrow, and tags.

All three leads got a next action, at 3 clicks plus text each. 'Set a reminder for the next action' takes a date (default tomorrow), an optional time and what you plan to do; the lead then shows 'You planned: 24/10/2026' and the list shows '1d'. An action due today needed another route: that lead stayed on To do and we added the action as a comment.
Moving a lead to 'Quotation sent' with the arrow in the step bar left its next action in place: the pipeline step and the next action are separate.

Typing an existing lead title in New lead showed '1 possible duplicate' with the reason 'Same title' before saving. The time in that warning was 2 hours off the time in the list, probably UTC against local time.
Keyboard shortcuts fire when you type outside a text field: once an edit screen and once a New lead window opened. Nothing was saved.

The 'New email' tab on a lead shows an invitation to connect a mailbox instead of an editor, so sending email from a lead needs that connection. The trial showed no limits per plan, so the app does not tell you which features sit above Starter.
not_tested: Mailbox, calendar or WhatsApp connections, and email from the lead
